If eps is exactly 0, #38 ties the ~350 x138 copies and sits behind the earlier ones, which is effectively a cliff. At p0 = 0.5, (a) 8/12 and (b) 4/12. At p0 = 1, (b) has the lowest cliff in 12/12 (0.056-0.196 vs 0.100-0.200) AND the highest E[max] in 12/12, so (a) is dominated whenever V*_C exists. So '(a) lowest or within 0.01 in 12/12', '(b) vs (a) is a coin flip' and '(c) higher cliff than (a) in 10/12' all depend on one unmodelled parameter. That is the I-092 false-precision failure again. So the 'transfer' world (+0.0006) has no support, and a public >= 0.955 from a DC neighbour says little about the ~71% private share. Re-offering it is allowed only as the user's choice, and the entry's reasoning against (c) (the L9 form) is exactly the part that fails the eps == 0 check. (5) Minor: the rungs themselves broke L5v2 (1) 'no threshold neighbours, no class C'. Making one a final compounds a post-hoc deviation, so the pre-score user letter is the only thing that keeps it honest. The eps scale is inconsistent (1e-4 in the arithmetic, ~1e-5 in the text). The user can see scores on Kaggle before the 10-min poll header, so the cutoff can slip by minutes (harmless if the letter is logged with date -u).
